title: Ethiopian Beetroot Salad
localName: ቀይ ስር ሰላጣ — Qey Sir Selata
community: Ethiopian fasting platters — the vivid purple salad
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Beetroot Salad — boiled beets sliced and dressed with lemon, oil, and garlic. The vivid purple salad of the Ethiopian fasting platter — its striking colour and earthy sweetness providing contrast against the red berbere stews.
longDesc: Ethiopian beetroot salad brings both visual drama and nutritional density to the fasting platter — the vivid purple beets dressed simply with lemon and garlic. It is one of the few completely raw (after boiling) elements of the Ethiopian table.
ingredients: ¼ cup fresh coriander or mint
steps: Boil beetroots 30—40 minutes until tender. Cool.
Peel. Slice into rounds or cubes.
Dress with lemon, oil, and garlic.
chefTips: Wear gloves when handling cooked beets — they stain deeply.
Room-temperature beets absorb the dressing better than cold.
commonMistakes: Not resting — the dressing needs time to penetrate.
cookingScience: Beetroot's red-purple colour comes from betalains — water-soluble pigments. Unlike anthocyanins (which turn blue in alkaline conditions and red in acid), betalains are stable across a wide pH range. The lemon juice enhances their brightness.
sustainabilityTips: Beets grow well in Ethiopian highlands.
healthBenefits: Nitrates from beets support cardiovascular health.
culturalNote: Beetroot salad brings the purple colour to the Ethiopian fasting platter — the visual completion of a table that already has red (Misir Wat), yellow (Kik Alicha), golden (Tikil Gomen), and green (Gomen). The Ethiopian fasting platter is edible art.
